prompt: The daylight in a northern town is modelled by $L(t) = 12 + 3\sin\left(\frac{2\pi (t - 80)}{365}\right)$ hours, where $t$ is the day of the year. How many hours of daylight does the longest day of the year have?
hint: The longest day happens when the sine part is as large as it can be.

hints.text: The longest day happens when the sine part is as large as it can be.
The largest value of any sine is $1$, so the most daylight is $12 + 3(1)$.

explanation: No matter what is inside it, a sine never exceeds $1$.
So the biggest $L(t)$ can be is $12 + 3(1) = 15$ hours.
The $-80$ inside only decides which day that happens on, not how big the maximum is.

alternativeExplanations.title: Read the parts of the model
steps: The $12$ is the midline: the yearly average is $12$ hours of daylight.
The $3$ is the amplitude: the town gains up to $3$ hours in summer and loses up to $3$ in winter.
Longest day $= 12 + 3 = 15$ hours; shortest day $= 12 - 3 = 9$ hours.
